biography: Patrick Beliën's racing journey began not on a pristine track, but on the rain-slicked cobblestone streets of his hometown in Flanders. As a teenager, he honed his skills drifting a battered Peugeot 205 through abandoned industrial estates, much to the dismay of local law enforcement. This raw, untamed talent caught the eye of a local racing enthusiast, who funded Beliën's entry into a regional karting series. His aggressive, no-holds-barred style quickly ruffled feathers, earning him both admirers and enemies. After a rapid ascent through the karting ranks, Beliën made the leap to GT racing, initially struggling with the precision required at higher levels. A pivotal moment came during a torrential downpour at Spa-Francorchamps, where he masterfully piloted a BMW M3 E46 GTR, overtaking three cars in a single lap to secure a podium finish. Now in his early thirties, Beliën continues to compete, driven by an insatiable hunger for victory.
drivingStyle: Beliën's driving style is best described as relentlessly aggressive. He attacks corners with a ferocity that often borders on reckless, maximizing every ounce of grip available. Tire management is not his forte; he prefers to push hard from the start, relying on raw speed to build a lead, often leaving his engineers wringing their hands as tire degradation sets in. Under pressure, Beliën thrives, transforming into an even more formidable competitor. He seems to relish the challenge of wheel-to-wheel combat, often making daring overtakes that leave spectators breathless.

rivalries.name: Alessandro Rossi
rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision that cost Rossi a championship victory in 2021. They have traded barbs and paint ever since.

rivalries.name: Ingrid Larsen
rivalries.reason: Beliën and Larsen have clashed repeatedly due to their contrasting driving philosophies. Larsen, known for her calculated precision, views Beliën's aggression as dangerous and undisciplined.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka and Beliën were teammates for a short period. Tanaka accused Beliën of unsportsmanlike behaviour by deliberately running him off the track during a practice session.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, no matter how worn.
Listens to classical music, specifically Bach, to calm his nerves before a race.
Has a small, worn teddy bear that he keeps in his driver's seat during every race.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Spa in 2022, after a nail-biting final stint where he held off a charging Rossi by just 0.3 seconds.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Nürburgring 24 Hours in 2020 due to a mechanical failure, costing his team a certain victory.
